summary: This article explains how kicking a football off-center makes it spin, why a spinning ball pushes on the air and bends in flight, and why a ball with no spin wobbles.
introduce: Show the title “The Science of a Curving Football Kick” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: how strongly something presses on a surface

challengeTerms.def: the act of turning around a center point
the curved path an object follows as it moves through the air or space
something that happens in nature that people can observe and study

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that scoring a great free kick depends more on science than on talent? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Use the words force and opposite to explain why a spinning football curves.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review force, pressure, and deflect, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses rotation, trajectory, and phenomenon to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
